The General Manager in charge of Engineering and Maintenance at Ghana Gas, Maxwell Caleb, has warned that Ghana could face power supply disruptions if illegal mining activities destroy gas pipelines connected to a gas processing plant at Prestea.
Speaking at a workshop organised for media personnel on energy reporting, Caleb cautioned that the continued practice of illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, poses a serious threat to critical energy infrastructure and the country’s power supply.
He stressed that the destruction of gas pipelines could disrupt the transportation of gas needed for electricity generation, potentially affecting power supply across the country.
According to him, the continued encroachment of illegal mining activities on areas around critical infrastructure could have far-reaching consequences for the energy sector if urgent measures are not taken to address the situation.
Caleb urged stakeholders to recognise the dangers associated with illegal mining and work together to protect energy installations from destruction.
He further emphasised that sustained illegal mining activities would not benefit the country, particularly when they threaten infrastructure that supports electricity generation and national development.
The workshop was organised to strengthen media personnel’s understanding of energy issues and improve reporting on developments within Ghana’s energy sector.
The warning comes amid continued concerns about the impact of illegal mining on the environment, public infrastructure and the country’s economic development.
Caleb’s remarks highlight the need for stronger collaboration among relevant authorities, security agencies, local communities and other stakeholders to safeguard critical gas infrastructure and prevent potential disruptions to electricity supply.
